newsitem.title: UK: BT firms after briefing, Warburg rates "buy".
newsitem.headline: BT firms after briefing, Warburg rates "buy".

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc shares turned slightly higher by mid session on Thursday after an upbeat presentation to analysts following yearly profits which were in line with expectations, dealers and analysts said.
The stock was up 2p at 451-1/2 by 1123 GMT in active trade of 7.5 million shares, after initially dropping 3-1/2p.
Analysts at SBC Warburg repeated a "buy" rating on BT following its post-results briefing, arguing that BT's growth prospects -- driven by new services such as video-on-demand -- were on track.

SBC pointed to a number of positive factors, which included an easing of the rate of BT price cuts in the current year as regulatory pressure relented. Also investment by BT's planned merger partner MCI should boost profits by 1999.

However Scruton said hopes for the MCI merger would probably underpin BT's shares for the immediate future. "I'm not a great fan of the MCI deal in terms of delivering higher earnings but I can't see the stock going down," he said.
"The fundamentals aren't good but the sentiment is good so we would be roughly neutral."
At Salomon Brothers, analyst Andrew Harrington also repeated a "hold" on BT, highlighting a a 2.7 percent drop in core UK revenues in the fourth quarter.
"That was at a time when the UK economy was very buoyant and the competition was busy merging," Harrington said. "Looking forward there is a significant increase in the competitive threat."
However Dennis Exton at Nikko Europe said the merger should produce a higher-growth group.
"It is a low-single-digit growth company transforming itself into a mid-teens growth company, and that is the story for the next three years," Exton said.

BT's annual pre-tax profit rose to 3.203 billion stg in the year ended March 31, from 3.019 billion a year before. Analysts' forecasts had mostly been in a range between 3.175 billion stg and 3.224 billion stg.
Encouraged by hopes for the MCI alliance, BT shares were trading some 28 percent above their level before the deal was announced on November 4.
